touch-id.title: Touch ID after reboot, plus a direct SEP check across suspend
touch-id.detail: Enrolment and verification work again after a reboot. A pending verify through /dev/sep-bio recovered across two suspend cycles. Suspend with the real lock screen and fprintd has not been tested.

touch-id.title: Touch ID after reboot
touch-id.detail: Reported to enrol and match after a reboot in SPI mode 2. This comes from a development branch.

thunderbolt.title: Thunderbolt dock: USB, display and resume
thunderbolt.detail: With the final 7.1.12-tbpr8-usb2fix2 build, a TS4 dock's USB2 attached on the first session in 3 of 3 tries, running a keyboard, a mouse and a 3840×2160 display at 120 Hz. Suspend to idle and Ethernet recovery on the TS4 were also reported. Not every dock or role swap was retested.

neural-engine.title: Neural Engine driver research (external module)
neural-engine.detail: On J293 the external module only binds. On J316C an encoder inference test matched its reference hash, but SET0 readback is still missing, and the Mac rebooted unexpectedly after a raw debug dump. The proposed kernel was never boot-tested.

touch-id.title: Touch ID after reboot
touch-id.detail: Matched after each of two separate reboots. With a Thunderbolt display connected, a bring-up retry recovered 2 of 4 boots. This PR did not test J316S.

thunderbolt.title: USB-C and Thunderbolt display, with resume
thunderbolt.detail: An LG UltraFine 5K ran at 3840×2160, 60 Hz and 10-bit from both left-hand ports. Plugging, replugging and a 10-second suspend to idle were tested. The M1 Max path was not tried on hardware.

neural-engine.title: Neural Engine driver research (external module)
neural-engine.detail: On J293 the external module only binds. On J316C an encoder inference test matched its reference hash, but SET0 readback is still missing, and the Mac rebooted unexpectedly after a raw debug dump. The proposed kernel was never boot-tested.

touch-id.title: Touch ID after reboot
touch-id.detail: Verified 3 times out of 3 after a reboot, using the commit-3 / test-11.5 work. The earlier enrolment work in #58 went into feat/sep, not the branch that was audited.

neural-engine.title: Neural Engine research (external driver)
neural-engine.detail: Programs ran, but about 1 result in 5 came back all zeros, across three boots, and unloading needed a reboot. It depends on a separate driver and an m1n1 firmware preload; it is not a packaged, supported path.

touch-id.title: Touch ID enrol, verify and sudo through PAM
touch-id.detail: An experimental PR reports this board. The J414C result from #69 does not carry over to J414S, and the separate profile work has not been integrated.

thunderbolt.title: Dual-dock display work
thunderbolt.detail: J414S (draft #46) sits on the review/pr14-base stack and J416C (#50) on the dual-dock branch. Both are development stacks; neither has been qualified on the merged working tree.

thunderbolt.title: USB devices through a Thunderbolt hub
thunderbolt.detail: A USB keyboard worked through an OWC Thunderbolt 5 hub. This does not cover DisplayPort or PCIe tunnelling.

thunderbolt.title: Thunderbolt display and resume work
thunderbolt.detail: This T602x board is the one tested in #8. The code also covers other Pro and Max laptops, but those boards have not been tested.

thunderbolt.title: Dual-dock display work
thunderbolt.detail: J414S (draft #46) sits on the review/pr14-base stack and J416C (#50) on the dual-dock branch. Both are development stacks; neither has been qualified on the merged working tree.

usb.title: USB 3 on every plug, replug and flip
usb.detail: A USB 3.2 Gen 1 stick came up at 5 Gbps in 6 of 6 attaches: each of the three USB-C ports, both cable orientations. The PHY coprocessor is stopped on every unplug and booted again on the next plug, as macOS does. Suspend with a USB 3 device attached, 10 Gbps and DisplayPort alt mode were not tested.

audio.title: Speakers, microphones and headphone jack
audio.detail: Tested by jgoyvaerts on his own J616s: the six speakers through the J616 speaker graph with speaker protection running, the three internal microphones and the headphone output. In Aurora as merged, the microphones and the jack card work, and the speakers stay locked until a speaker protection config for the J616s ships. The headset microphone and the jack across a suspend were not tested.

graphics.title: Ray tracing on 25G83 with #837 and mesa#139
graphics.detail: With both open patches on jgoyvaerts's J616s (Mesa ec38aea3): the Vulkan CTS ray-query, ray-tracing-pipeline and acceleration structure groups ran 74,833 cases, 49,711 Pass, 25,122 NotSupported, 0 Fail, 0 GPU recoveries. A ray tracing demo with 16.8 M instanced triangles ran 1,337 frames at about 53 fps. Compute jobs stop at 38.9 s, and a long fragment traversal freezes the desktop: 14 s passed, 28 s failed. Proton, vkd3d and ray tracing pipelines on the x86 driver were not tested.

graphics.title: GPU enabled on the J616s
graphics.detail: The calibrated 20-core GPU is on in Aurora as merged: the boot loader fills in the per-chip values, and the kernel refuses the GPU if they are missing. On the preceding stack Vulkan reported Apple M4 Pro (G16S B1), vkcube ran, glmark2-es2 scored 6271 and a ten-minute soak had no GPU or DART faults. jgoyvaerts runs the desktop on it daily (OpenGL 4.6, Vulkan 1.4). Vulkan is not formally conformant.

graphics.title: GPU on the G17 backend with Mesa as G17P
graphics.detail: Tested by jgoyvaerts on his own J616s with per-unit values his boot loader fills in: the M4 Pro GPU (25G83 firmware) drives the desktop, vkmark completes all 13 scenes and glmark2 runs with no GPU recovery or fault. In Aurora as merged, the J616s GPU stays disabled until m1n1 fills in per-chip calibration, and the Mesa side (mesa#55) is still open. Ray tracing is refused on 25G83.

suspend.title: RTC wake, Wi-Fi and the Neural Engine
suspend.detail: rtcwake on the PMU RTC suspended and woke the machine 3 of 3 times (#836). 21 of 21 RTC cycles with the Neural Engine up brought Wi-Fi back in 1.3 to 3.4 s with no bus errors, and Bluetooth stayed up (#854). On jgoyvaerts's J616s, last run 2026-10-30, a lid sleep woke cleanly but the speakers stayed silent until speakersafetyd restarted (#820). Battery drain over a long sleep was not measured.

suspend.title: Suspend to idle by lid and menu
suspend.detail: The lid and the menu put the machine into suspend to idle; opening the lid wakes it and the keyboard and trackpad work after resume. The keyboard only wakes the system on real input (#409). Battery drain over a long sleep was not measured.

display.title: Panel at 120 Hz with HDR
display.detail: The panel runs at 120 Hz through the display coprocessor. HDR reaches the 1600 nit peak under GNOME 51 (#553) and a PQ reference white keeps headroom for HDR content (#789). On jgoyvaerts's J616s under Hyprland (7.3.0-m4.102), mpv passes HDR10 through to the panel: the backlight rail drew 9.83 W on PQ 1600 bars against 5.47 W for the same bars without HDR. HDR across a sleep, screen sharing and HDR on battery were not tested.

touch-id.title: Touch ID enrolment and match
touch-id.detail: The Secure Enclave attaches warm, fprintd lists the sensor, and an enrolled finger matched in fprintd-verify and kept matching after later reboots. After a Stage 1 reinstall, a one-time allowance brought Touch ID and the enrolled finger back (#545). A second Stage 1 change with no manual step was not tested, and this was not repeated on jgoyvaerts's J616s.

neural-engine.title: MobileNet on the M4 Pro Neural Engine
neural-engine.detail: MobileNetV1 got 16 of 16 images right at 0.68 ms per image (macOS Core ML: 0.30 ms), add-128 was exact, and 12 load cycles passed. The remaining speed gap is most likely the DRAM rail. Not repeated on jgoyvaerts's J616s.

boot.title: RAM boot and restart with the J873g platform series
boot.detail: Tested by Acelogic on a J873g. Guarded RAM boots through aura main (1.0.0b9) with the J873g platform series (linux#1197, now in aurora-wip): every boot check passed, the GPU smoke rendered correct pixels and the kernel stayed untainted. Restart through the SMC (reboot -f with macsmc-reboot) brought the Mac back through iBoot into aura three times, with no boot error left in the PMU. Power-off was not tested.

boot.title: Linux from the SSD through aura, without a host
boot.detail: Tested by Thomas Glanzmann on his own J873g. aura brings up the USB, Wi-Fi/Bluetooth and PCIe hardware itself, reads the kernel, device tree and initramfs from an EFI system partition on the internal SSD and boots Linux with all 12 CPUs, USB, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and both displays. aura is still chainloaded from the installed stage 1 over the USB debug link for this. The aura side is now in aura main (aura#16); Linux's own SSD support is in aurora-wip (linux#1197).

cpu.title: All CPU performance states
cpu.detail: Tested by Thomas Glanzmann on his own J873g, booted through the m1n1/aura proxy. All twelve cores run every performance state (P/M up to 4.79 GHz, E up to 2.94 GHz) with load-driven governors, after the fix for the WFxT erratum that corrupted data. The SMC leaves the fan at its minimum, so a fan control service was part of the same change; stress-ng on all 12 cores reached 82 C with the fan at about 4500 RPM. Not in the public kernel: apple-soc-cpufreq keeps the J873g at two states per cluster until a thermal policy exists, so the public kernel (linux#1197) leaves the higher states out.

cpu.title: All 12 cores with bounded frequency scaling
cpu.detail: Linux runs on all twelve CPUs, with two performance states per cluster (972/1152 MHz E, 1440/1728 MHz P/M).

storage.title: Read-only SSD probe on the public port
storage.detail: Tested by Acelogic with linux#1197, now in aurora-wip, read-only: the controller comes up with its namespaces, the partition table and direct reads work, and removing the driver sends the shutdown notification. No writes were made.

storage.title: Internal SSD
storage.detail: Tested by Thomas Glanzmann on his own J873g, booted through the m1n1/aura proxy. The ANS2 controller with the T8152 register layout: fio reaches 3.8 GiB/s sequential read, 2.9 GiB/s sequential write and 140k IOPS 4K random read on ext4. With the power-off series the SSD reports a clean shutdown on the next boot. Ported to aurora-wip in linux#1197 (merged), where write testing has not been repeated.

usb.title: USB 2 hosts in aurora-wip
usb.detail: Tested by Acelogic with linux#1205: both hosts bind as apple,t8152-dwc3, the on-board hub behind the front ports enumerates at high speed, and a USB HID device in a front port enumerated behind it at full speed. A device plugged in while the hub is runtime-suspended is only seen once the hub resumes.

usb.title: USB 2 on the back-left and front ports
usb.detail: Tested by Thomas Glanzmann on his own J873g, booted through the m1n1/aura proxy. A keyboard and an RTL8153 USB Ethernet adapter work on the front ports (behind the on-board VL822 hub), a keyboard on the back-left port, at high speed. The loader has to wake the back-left port controller and release the hub reset first, which aura main does (aura#16). USB 3, the back-middle and back-right ports and Thunderbolt are not supported. Now in aurora-wip through linux#1205, which describes the hosts as apple,t8152-dwc3.

ethernet.title: 10GbE driver on the public port
ethernet.detail: Tested by Acelogic with linux#1197, now in aurora-wip: the on-board NIC (it identifies as RTL8125CP) binds and its PHY attaches. No cable was connected, so traffic was not tested.

ethernet.title: On-board 10GbE
ethernet.detail: Tested by Thomas Glanzmann on his own J873g, booted through the m1n1/aura proxy. TCP runs at 9.4 Gbit/s in both directions at MTU 1500 once the link is retrained to 16 GT/s (from userspace for now). Keeping the read request size at 512 bytes matters for sending: UDP out is 8.9 Gbit/s at 512 and 7.9 at 4096 (five paired runs each). Ported to aurora-wip in linux#1197 (merged); the r8169 transmit changes are in linux#1198 (draft).

display.title: USB-C display on the back-right port
display.detail: Tested by Acelogic on a J873g. aura brings up the back-right USB-C display from a cold boot at 1280x720 and hands Linux its framebuffer; this is in aura main (aura#16). The Linux display driver is still a draft (linux#1019).

hdmi.title: HDMI and dual display
hdmi.detail: Tested by Thomas Glanzmann on his own J873g, booted through the m1n1/aura proxy. HDMI through the dptx-phy and the Parade PS190 converter at 2560x1440 next to the USB-C display at 1280x720; Linux gets both as framebuffers. This is now in aura main (aura#16). Mode changes after boot and hotplug are not supported.

audio.title: Headphone jack on the public port; speaker held off
audio.detail: Tested by Acelogic with linux#1197, now in aurora-wip: the sound card registers, silent playback and capture on the headphone jack work, and the speaker stays disabled. aura#115 (draft) passes the speaker amp's configuration from the ADT, which speaker protection needs.

audio.title: Speaker and headphone jack
audio.detail: Tested by Thomas Glanzmann on his own J873g, booted through the m1n1/aura proxy. Playback works on the headphone jack and on the internal speaker. The speaker stays off unless explicitly enabled, until a speaker protection profile for the J873g exists. The headset microphone was not tested. Ported to aurora-wip in linux#1197 (merged).

graphics.title: OpenGL on Mesa aurora-wip
graphics.detail: Tested by Acelogic on a J873g: Mesa aurora-wip, which includes mesa#175, renders on Apple M6 (G18G) with the G18 kernel backend (linux#984). The GPU smoke and texture LOD tests pass with correct pixels, also with mesa#178. No full conformance run on this stack yet.

wifi.title: N1 Wi-Fi on aurora-wip
wifi.detail: Tested by Acelogic on a J873g: the native N1 Wi-Fi scans, joins a WPA2 network and ran 10 minutes of two-way TCP at a 30 Mbit/s cap (linux#1013, with linux#998). Suspend was not tested.

bluetooth.title: Bluetooth LE discovery
bluetooth.detail: Tested by Acelogic on a J873g with linux#1013: LE discovery alongside Wi-Fi traffic. Pairing, ACL and audio were not tested.

suspend.title: Suspend to idle by lid and menu
suspend.detail: With the display sleep handshake (#830) and USB wake (#832), the Mac sleeps from the menu and the lid and wakes on the keyboard, trackpad, power button, lid or a USB device on either port. Display, GPU, Wi-Fi and audio come back. Over 148 s asleep the CPUs woke 3 times, against 1472 times in 938 s before the mailbox change. Battery drain over a long sleep was not measured.

touch-id.title: Touch ID enrolment and match
touch-id.detail: On a J713 on 26.6.2 firmware, the Secure Enclave attached, fprintd enrolled a finger in 10 stages and matched it, and the enrolment came back and matched after a reboot. The lock screen unlocked through pam_fprintd. The installer does not collect the J713 sensor root key and calibration yet.

thunderbolt.title: USB4 dock with Ethernet and two 4K displays
thunderbolt.detail: With a CalDigit TS5 dock, the link came up as 2 x 20 Gb/s USB4 at boot and on hotplug in both orientations, and the dock Ethernet ran at 2.3 Gbit/s over the PCIe tunnel (#846). Two monitors ran at 3840x2160 at 60 Hz through DisplayPort tunnels, survived replug, and came back after suspend to idle. Other docks, HBR3 and sleep power with the dock attached were not tested.

audio.title: Microphones, headphone jack and speakers in the kernel
audio.detail: On a J713 test kernel, all three sound cards registered. The microphones recorded, the jack played left and right correctly with plug detection, and the speakers played with speaker protection running. The J713 speaker protection profile, UCM and DSP graph are still open, so a stock install keeps the speakers locked.

graphics.title: 32-core GPU on 25G83 firmware
graphics.detail: On AxxzyWasTaken's J616C (14-core CPU, 32-core GPU, 25G83 firmware), a private 7.3 tree with #1050, the larger clustering metadata and a 96-block render pool runs the Hyprland desktop and x86 games under FEX; SCP:SL held about 117 fps at its cap, and 55 of 55 offscreen tests passed. Not as merged: #1050 is still open, and upstream's 44-block pool is untested here.

graphics.title: 40-core GPU on the M4 Max
graphics.detail: With the driver (#958) and Mesa (mesa#85), 20 gpu-niri replays, 10 minutes of mixed rendering and 123 whisper.cpp runs finished with no GPU recoveries. HEVC decoding matched software decoding on 4 of 4 samples. The GPU uses a static calibration from one part and stays off in the merged device tree until the boot loader handoff lands. CTS, sustained load and suspend were not qualified.

touch-id.title: Touch ID unlock on 7.3
touch-id.detail: On AxxzyWasTaken's J616C (14-core CPU, 32-core GPU, 25G83 firmware), the lock screen unlocked from a finger in about 2 s with libfprint-aurora 1.94.100-3, which handles the v5 interface. Two lock and unlock cycles in a row worked after a reboot. Not tested through the installer.

touch-id.title: Touch ID enrolment and match
touch-id.detail: A new finger enrolled and matched, and after a reboot both enrolled identities came back and matched again. Unlocking with Touch ID worked. sudo and the installer path were not tested.

neural-engine.title: Neural Engine startup on a 32-core M4 Max
neural-engine.detail: On AxxzyWasTaken's J616C (14-core CPU, 32-core GPU, 25G83 firmware), startup completed on 40 of 44 boots. The 4 failures match the H16 stall that #1066 restarts; two of them fell in boots with other faults, and the restart path has not run here yet. This part's preload is not admitted upstream yet. No inference job was run.

neural-engine.title: Neural Engine on the M4 Max
neural-engine.detail: A conv3x3 test matched the macOS reference over 200 runs with no faults. It needs a boot loader handoff that fills and enables the Neural Engine nodes. Long runs and the MobileNet test were not measured.

audio.title: Speakers and microphones on the M4 Max
audio.detail: On AxxzyWasTaken's J616C (14-core CPU, 32-core GPU, 25G83 firmware) and a private 7.3 tree: three sound cards, the J616 speaker graph with speaker protection running and volumes unlocked, and the microphone filter. AUX2 is silent here, so only AUX0 and AUX1 are mixed. The tuning work is in asahi-audio#14, still open. Speaker protection values for this model were not measured.

suspend.title: s2idle overnight on the M4 Max
suspend.detail: On AxxzyWasTaken's J616C (14-core CPU, 32-core GPU, 25G83 firmware): lid closed unplugged for 8.48 h, 3284 to 1932 mAh, 1.83 W on average, one clean suspend and a wake on lid with no errors. A timed wake on the PMU RTC also worked. This is s2idle, not deep sleep; macOS is about 0.1 W.

wifi.title: Wi-Fi on a private 7.3 tree
wifi.detail: On AxxzyWasTaken's J616C (14-core CPU, 32-core GPU, 25G83 firmware), a private 7.3 tree: the BCM4388 joins at 5 GHz with an 80 MHz channel and is in daily use. Not as merged, and no throughput or suspend test was recorded.

camera.title: Camera capture with the ISP enabled
camera.detail: On AxxzyWasTaken's J616C (14-core CPU, 32-core GPU, 25G83 firmware), a 7.3 kernel with the loader handoff (aura#71, merged) and an earlier version of the device tree change (#1368, still open): the camera came up as FaceTime HD Camera at 1920x1080, and a 6-second capture gave a live image, checked by its brightness only.

bluetooth.title: Bluetooth on a private 7.3 tree
bluetooth.detail: On AxxzyWasTaken's J616C (14-core CPU, 32-core GPU, 25G83 firmware), a private 7.3 tree: the adapter comes up and plays to an audio output. No long test was run.

boot.title: Preliminary (untested) installer support
boot.detail: The installer admits this Mac as experimental. Nobody on the team has one yet, so nothing has been tested on hardware. The kernel device tree is preliminary, the touchscreen and the glowing Apple logo do not work yet, and the OLED panel works only as a boot screen until the display driver supports it.

boot.detail: The installer admits this Mac as experimental. Nobody on the team has one yet, so nothing has been tested on hardware. The kernel device tree is preliminary, the touchscreen and the glowing Apple logo do not work yet, and the OLED panel works only as a boot screen until the display driver supports it.

The kernel device tree is preliminary, the touchscreen and the glowing Apple logo do not work yet, and the OLED panel works only as a boot screen until the display driver supports it.

The kernel device tree is preliminary, the touchscreen and the glowing Apple logo do not work yet, and the OLED panel works only as a boot screen until the display driver supports it.

boot.title: J704 boots on hardware
boot.detail: dmitzsaz booted his J704 on the macOS 27.0 stub with aurora-wip plus linux#1060, #1122, #1123 and #1124. CPU frequency scaling, NVMe, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, the SD reader, keyboard and trackpad, USB, the SMC and s2idle worked. The internal display stayed on the boot framebuffer.

display.title: Internal display stays on the boot framebuffer
display.detail: On the J704 the display coprocessor does not take over the panel, so it stays on the boot framebuffer. quank123wip saw the same coprocessor fail with -110 on the macOS 27.0 stub.
